literature.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期尼帕病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 校准后的参数被转换为空间系统中的密度基量。通过标准化的多高斯热点启动的模拟显示,局部暴发在扩散驱动下发生扩散,感染人类和感染果蝠的密度显著衰减,而水果中的感染则相对持续。 [10.1007/s12190-026-02940-7]
结果表明,融合前NiVF的较高基础灵活性展示了病毒进入诱导所需的构象亚稳性,而NiVG-受体界面则呈现为一个刚性且稳定的中和抗体靶标。 [10.3390/biophysica6060118]

本研究鉴定了1116个在至少一个时间点差异表达的基因,以及1677个表现出显著时间表达模式的基因,定义了一个包含516个基因的核心时间宿主响应特征。该特征捕捉了从早期病毒相关识别到炎症信号、内质网应激、蛋白质加工需求增加以及细胞周期和DNA复制失调的阶段性转变。综合筛选共获得38个候选药物,其中二甲双胍(metformin)、非诺贝特(fenofibrate)、洛纳法瑞宾(lonafarnib)和丙磺舒(probenecid)被优先选择用于进一步的实验验证。 [10.3390/cimb48111246]
综述得出结论,尼帕病毒(NiV)是一种具有高病例死亡率和广泛宿主范围的人兽共患病(zoonotic)病毒,对全球健康构成重大威胁。它强调了野生动物宿主(储存宿主)、环境变化和人类-动物接触面之间的复杂相互作用,这些因素驱动了印度次大陆的反复暴发(暴发)。综述还强调了需要采用One Health方法以增强监测(监测)和准备能力。 [10.3390/microorganisms14112691]
在此研究中,乙酰转移酶NAT10被鉴定为NiV出芽的关键驱动因子。 [10.1002/advs.78901]

The results indicate that the higher baseline flexibility of pre-fusion NiVF demonstrates conformational metastability necessary for viral entry induction, whereas the NiVG-receptor interface presents a rigid, stable target for neutralizing antibodies. [10.3390/biophysica6060118]

The study identified 1116 differentially expressed genes at one or more time points and 1677 genes with significant temporal expression patterns, defining a 516-gene core temporal host-response signature. [10.3390/cimb48111246]
The review concludes that NiV is a zoonotic henipavirus with a high case–fatality ratio and a broad host range, posing a significant global health threat. [10.3390/microorganisms14112691]
Here, the acetyltransferase NAT10 is identified as a critical driver of NiV budding. [10.1002/advs.78901]

papers.title: Re-Emergence of Nipah Virus in the Indian Subcontinent: From Immune Evasion to Transmission Dynamics, Risk Assessment and One Health Preparedness
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic henipavirus with a high case–fatality ratio and a broad host range, posing a significant global health threat due to its potential for recurrent spillover and human transmission. Since its first outbreak in Malaysia in 1998, the epidemiology of NiV has evolved through repeated outbreaks across Southeast Asia, particularly in the Indian subcontinent, driven by complex interactions among wildlife reservoirs, environmental changes, and expanding human–animal interfaces. This review discusses the molecular biology, pathogenesis, host immune responses, and immune evasion strategies of NiV, as well as the anthropogenic and ecological factors involved in the spillover, transmission, and epidemiology of NiV in South Asia. It also explores ecological and epidemiological considerations for the surveillance and preparedness for NiV in China and differentiates established virological evidence and hypothesis-generating observations. We also explore the ecological and anthropogenic factors contributing to the spillover, spread, and changing epidemiology of NiV in South Asia, with a particular focus on environmental and climatic, as well as socioecological, factors that have driven recurrent outbreaks. A conceptual, hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing ecological surveillance in China is discussed, considering reservoir–host distribution, cross-border connectivity, environmental suitability, and wildlife–livestock–human interfaces. The review also examines recent developments in antiviral therapeutics, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccine development, and highlights research gaps that remain to be addressed to achieve successful prevention and control. Lastly, this review suggests a One Health approach that combines surveillance of wildlife, veterinary, environmental, and human health and is grounded in a multidisciplinary framework to enhance early detection, boost regional preparedness, and facilitate evidence-based public health decision-making.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on Nipah virus (NiV) infection and disease, examining its molecular biology, pathogenesis, immune evasion strategies, and the ecological and anthropogenic factors driving its spillover, transmission, and changing epidemiology in South Asia. The central question is to understand the mechanisms of NiV emergence, transmission dynamics, and risk factors for outbreaks, with an emphasis on the Indian subcontinent.

papers.title_zh: 印度次大陆尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒)的再次出现:从免疫逃逸到病毒动态、风险评估及One Health准备
papers.source_body_en: Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic henipavirus with a high case–fatality ratio and a broad host range, posing a significant global health threat due to its potential for recurrent spillover and human transmission. Since its first outbreak in Malaysia in 1998, the epidemiology of NiV has evolved through repeated outbreaks across Southeast Asia, particularly in the Indian subcontinent, driven by complex interactions among wildlife reservoirs, environmental changes, and expanding human–animal interfaces. This review discusses the molecular biology, pathogenesis, host immune responses, and immune evasion strategies of NiV, as well as the anthropogenic and ecological factors involved in the spillover, transmission, and epidemiology of NiV in South Asia. It also explores ecological and epidemiological considerations for the surveillance and preparedness for NiV in China and differentiates established virological evidence and hypothesis-generating observations. We also explore the ecological and anthropogenic factors contributing to the spillover, spread, and changing epidemiology of NiV in South Asia, with a particular focus on environmental and climatic, as well as socioecological, factors that have driven recurrent outbreaks. A conceptual, hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing ecological surveillance in China is discussed, considering reservoir–host distribution, cross-border connectivity, environmental suitability, and wildlife–livestock–human interfaces. The review also examines recent developments in antiviral therapeutics, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccine development, and highlights research gaps that remain to be addressed to achieve successful prevention and control. Lastly, this review suggests a One Health approach that combines surveillance of wildlife, veterinary, environmental, and human health and is grounded in a multidisciplinary framework to enhance early detection, boost regional preparedness, and facilitate evidence-based public health decision-making.
papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒,NiV)是一种人兽共患病(zoonotic)病毒,具有高病例死亡率和广泛的宿主范围,由于其可能引发反复暴发(跨物种溢出)和人类传播(传播),对全球健康构成重大威胁。自1998年马来西亚首次暴发(暴发)以来,尼帕病毒(NiV)的流行(流行病学)通过东南亚地区,特别是印度次大陆的多次暴发(暴发)而演变,这种演变是由野生动物宿主(储存宿主)、环境变化以及人类与动物接触面的扩展之间的复杂相互作用驱动的。本综述讨论了尼帕病毒(NiV)的分子生物学、传播(发病机制)、宿主(宿主)范围和免疫逃逸策略,以及南亚地区尼帕病毒(NiV)暴发(跨物种溢出)、传播(传播)和流行(流行病学)变化所涉及的人为和生态因素。此外,还探讨了中国及其他地区尼帕病毒(NiV)的生态和流行病学考量,以及监测(监测)和应对准备,并区分了已建立的病毒学证据和产生假设的观察结果。我们还探讨了导致南亚地区尼帕病毒(NiV)暴发(跨物种溢出)、传播和流行(流行病学)变化的生态和人为因素,特别关注环境和气候因素,以及社会生态因素。本综述还讨论了一个概念性的、产生假设的框架,用于在中国优先考虑生态监测(监测),考虑野生动物宿主(储存宿主)与宿主(宿主)的分布、跨境连通性、环境适宜性和野生动物-家畜-人类接触面。综述还探讨了近期在抗病毒药物(抗病毒药物)治疗、单克隆抗体和疫苗(疫苗)开发方面的进展,并突出了仍需解决的研究空白,以实现有效的预防和控制。最后,本综述建议采用One Health方法,结合野生动物、兽医、环境和人类健康的监测(监测),并基于跨学科框架,以增强早期检测、提升区域准备能力,并促进基于证据的公共卫生决策。

papers.title: Structural Aspects of Nipah Virus Glycoproteins Using Predictive Protein Modeling
papers.abstract: Nipah is a virus-borne zoonotic disease that mostly occurs in Southeast Asian countries. Nipah virus (NiV) infection is potentially lethal as it can cause fatal encephalitis, and as of now, there are no vaccines or therapeutic treatments for this disease. The highly pathogenic NiV belongs to the paramyxovirus family, and the natural host of NiV is fruit bats of the Pteropodidae family. Though NiV has not been detected in the US, the Camp Hill virus (CHV), which is characteristically similar to Nipah and shares the henipavirus group with NiV, was recently identified in Camp Hill, Alabama. The present paper describes the structures of these viral glycoproteins using the available database of protein structures, and examines if they have an evolutionary link to other viral glycoproteins. Certain similar glycoproteins found in different countries are also explored. The structure–function relationships for these two NiV glycoproteins are determined using time-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The interfacial ligand–receptor interactions between the NiVG–ephrinB2 receptor and NiVF–monoclonal antibody (Fab66) complexes are examined. The results indicate that the higher baseline flexibility of pre-fusion NiVF (truncated in this case) demonstrates conformational metastability necessary for viral entry induction, whereas the NiVG-receptor interface presents a rigid, stable target for neutralizing antibodies. Possible evolutionary relationships of these viral glycoproteins, along with related emerging zoonotic viruses, are examined through phylogenetic analyses. A primary motivation for these structural studies is that these results might contribute to future therapeutic developments and drug designs to effectively combat NiV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic disease that occurs primarily in Southeast Asian countries, and it is potentially lethal, causing fatal encephalitis with no current vaccines or treatments available.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focuses on the structural aspects of Nipah virus glycoproteins using predictive protein modeling, examining their evolutionary links to other viral glycoproteins and exploring similar glycoproteins found in different countries.
analysis.methods: The structure–function relationships for the two NiV glycoproteins are determined using time-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and interfacial ligand–receptor interactions between the NiVG–ephrinB2 receptor and NiVF–monoclonal antibody (Fab66) complexes are analyzed.
analysis.main_results: The results indicate that the higher baseline flexibility of pre-fusion NiVF demonstrates conformational metastability necessary for viral entry induction, whereas the NiVG-receptor interface presents a rigid, stable target for neutralizing antibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the structural findings provide insights into the mechanisms of NiV entry and neutralization, which could be novel for understanding the virus's behavior and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform future therapeutic developments and drug designs to effectively combat Nipah virus infection and related diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to structural analysis and does not include experimental validation, which may affect the strength of the evidence, but the use of molecular dynamics simulation provides a moderate level of confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural aspects of Nipah virus glycoproteins using predictive protein modeling and molecular dynamics simulations. It examines the conformational flexibility of NiVF and the stability of the NiVG-receptor interface, which are critical for viral entry and neutralization. The findings suggest that these structural features could inform future therapeutic developments. The study is limited to computational analysis without experimental validation, which may affect the strength of the evidence, but the approach provides a moderate level of confidence. The research highlights the importance of understanding glycoprotein structures for combating Nipah virus infection and related diseases.

papers.title_zh: 利用预测蛋白质建模研究尼帕病毒糖蛋白的结构特征
papers.source_body_en: Nipah is a virus-borne zoonotic disease that mostly occurs in Southeast Asian countries. Nipah virus (NiV) infection is potentially lethal as it can cause fatal encephalitis, and as of now, there are no vaccines or therapeutic treatments for this disease. The highly pathogenic NiV belongs to the paramyxovirus family, and the natural host of NiV is fruit bats of the Pteropodidae family. Though NiV has not been detected in the US, the Camp Hill virus (CHV), which is characteristically similar to Nipah and shares the henipavirus group with NiV, was recently identified in Camp Hill, Alabama. The present paper describes the structures of these viral glycoproteins using the available database of protein structures, and examines if they have an evolutionary link to other viral glycoproteins. Certain similar glycoproteins found in different countries are also explored. The structure–function relationships for these two NiV glycoproteins are determined using time-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The interfacial ligand–receptor interactions between the NiVG–ephrinB2 receptor and NiVF–monoclonal antibody (Fab66) complexes are examined. The results indicate that the higher baseline flexibility of pre-fusion NiVF (truncated in this case) demonstrates conformational metastability necessary for viral entry induction, whereas the NiVG-receptor interface presents a rigid, stable target for neutralizing antibodies. Possible evolutionary relationships of these viral glycoproteins, along with related emerging zoonotic viruses, are examined through phylogenetic analyses. A primary motivation for these structural studies is that these results might contribute to future therapeutic developments and drug designs to effectively combat NiV.
papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒是一种通过病毒传播的人兽共患病,主要发生在东南亚国家。尼帕病毒(NiV)感染具有潜在致命性,因为它可能导致致命的脑炎,目前尚无疫苗或治疗性治疗。高度致病性的NiV属于副粘病毒科,其天然储存宿主是宿主的果蝠。尽管NiV在美国尚未被检测到,但最近在阿拉巴马州坎普希尔发现了一种特征上与尼帕病毒相似且与NiV同属亨尼帕病毒类群的坎普希尔病毒(CHV)。本文利用现有的蛋白质结构数据库描述了这些病毒糖蛋白的结构,并探讨它们是否与其他病毒糖蛋白存在进化联系。同时,还研究了不同国家中发现的某些相似糖蛋白。通过基于时间的分子动力学(MD)模拟,确定了这两种NiV糖蛋白的结构-功能关系。研究分析了NiVG与ephrinB2受体以及NiVF与单克隆抗体(Fab66)复合物之间的界面配体-受体相互作用。结果表明,融合前NiVF(在此情况下为截断形式)的较高基础灵活性展示了病毒进入诱导所需的构象亚稳性,而NiVG-受体界面则呈现为一个刚性且稳定的中和抗体靶标。通过系统发育分析,探讨了这些病毒糖蛋白可能的进化关系,以及与相关新兴人兽共患病病毒的联系。这些结构研究的主要动机是,这些结果可能有助于未来针对NiV的治疗性药物开发和设计。

papers.full_text: Abstract Nipah virus transmission is governed by interacting host, environmental, and spatial processes that are not adequately represented by purely temporal compartmental models. This study formulates a two-dimensional reaction–diffusion model describing transmission among human, fruit, and fruit-bat populations, with fruit-mediated and cross-species infection pathways, demographic processes, recovery, mortality, immunity loss, and spatial transport. Cumulative reported cases from Bangladesh over the period 2001–2024 are used to calibrate the human transmission coefficients through bounded nonlinear least-squares estimation applied to the corresponding nonspatial count-based model. Consistent scaling relations are then employed to convert the calibrated parameters into density-based quantities for the spatial system. The disease-free equilibrium and the basic reproduction number are derived using the next-generation matrix approach. The threshold quantity is determined by the maximum of the human, fruit, and fruit-bat reproduction components. Under the assumptions of non-negative uniformly bounded solutions and equal diffusion coefficients within each population group, the disease-free equilibrium is proved to be globally asymptotically stable when \(\mathcal{R}_{0} < 1\). The directional transmission structure also leads to distinct human-only, human–fruit, and full spatially homogeneous endemic equilibria under population-specific threshold conditions. A Crank–Nicolson Lie-splitting finite-difference scheme is developed for the numerical approximation, with first-order temporal and second-order spatial accuracy. Simulations initiated by normalized multiple-Gaussian hotspots show diffusion-driven broadening of localized outbreaks, substantial decay of infected-human and infected fruit-bat densities, and comparatively persistent infection in the fruit compartment. Normalized sensitivity indices identify transmission and recruitment parameters as positive drivers of the reproduction components, whereas mortality, recovery, and fruit-removal parameters exert negative effects. The proposed framework provides a data-informed spatial description of Nipah virus transmission and clarifies the role of fruit-mediated infection in sustaining spatial persistence. papers.title_original: A robust study of multi-species nipah virus transmission via spatial reaction-diffusion modeling with real data

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study was needed to better understand the spatial dynamics of Nipah virus transmission, which are not adequately captured by purely temporal compartmental models. The research aimed to formulate a spatial reaction-diffusion model that incorporates host, environmental, and spatial interactions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a two-dimensional reaction–diffusion model to describe transmission among human, fruit, and fruit-bat populations, including pathways for fruit-mediated and cross-species infections, demographic processes, recovery, mortality, immunity loss, and spatial transport. The model was calibrated using cumulative reported cases from Bangladesh over the period 2001–2024.
analysis.methods: The model parameters were calibrated using bounded nonlinear least-squares estimation applied to a nonspatial count-based model. Consistent scaling relations were then used to convert the calibrated parameters into density-based quantities for the spatial system. A Crank–Nicolson Lie-splitting finite-difference scheme was developed for numerical approximation with first-order temporal and second-order spatial accuracy.
analysis.main_results: The calibrated parameters were converted into density-based quantities for the spatial system. Simulations initiated by normalized multiple-Gaussian hotspots showed diffusion-driven broadening of localized outbreaks, substantial decay of infected-human and infected fruit-bat densities, and comparatively persistent infection in the fruit compartment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the role of fruit-mediated infection in sustaining spatial persistence of Nipah virus. The study's novelty lies in its data-informed spatial description of Nipah virus transmission, which clarifies the dynamics of the disease across different populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies for Nipah virus by highlighting the importance of spatial factors in disease spread. papers.title: Time-Resolved Host Transcriptomics and Network Proximity Prioritize Host-Directed Candidate Drugs for Nipah Virus Infection
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic henipavirus that causes severe respiratory and neurological disease, yet no specific therapeutics are approved for human NiV infection. Because studies involving live NiV require biosafety level 4 containment and are technically demanding, computational host-directed drug repositioning provides a practical strategy for prioritizing candidates before experimental validation. Using the public NiV infection transcriptomic dataset GSE166707, we developed a time-resolved host-response drug-repositioning framework that integrated time-point differential expression analysis with time-series modeling. Core temporal genes were stratified into host dependency factors, host restriction factors and residual host-response genes using annotations from the Human–Virus Interaction DataBase. Candidate drugs were prioritized by combining Connectivity Map (CMap) reversal analysis, network proximity analysis, literature-curated NiV host-pathway directionality, pharmacological suitability and reported antiviral evidence. Suitable public drug-perturbation transcriptomic datasets were further analyzed by gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) to evaluate their consistency with the predicted reversal directions. We identified 1116 genes differentially expressed at one or more time points and 1677 genes exhibiting significant temporal expression patterns, whose intersection defined a 516-gene core temporal host-response signature comprising 58 host dependency factors, 18 host restriction factors and 440 residual host-response genes. This signature captured a staged transition from early virus-associated recognition to inflammatory signaling, endoplasmic reticulum stress, increased protein-processing demands, and dysregulation of the cell cycle and DNA replication. Integrated screening yielded 38 candidate drugs, from which metformin, fenofibrate, lonafarnib and probenecid were prioritized as host-directed candidates warranting further experimental validation. Gene-level reversal and host-network analyses revealed drug-specific modulation of NiV-associated host programs, while external drug-perturbation GSEA supported selected host-factor reversal patterns for metformin and fenofibrate. Overall, this framework provides a reproducible strategy for prioritizing host-directed therapeutic candidates against NiV infection.

The research did not involve live NiV and was conducted using computational methods.
analysis.methods: The research integrated time-point differential expression analysis with time-series modeling to stratify core temporal genes into host dependency factors, host restriction factors, and residual host-response genes. Connectivity Map (CMap) reversal analysis, network proximity analysis, literature-curated NiV host-pathway directionality, pharmacological suitability, and reported antiviral evidence were used to prioritize candidate drugs.
analysis.main_results: The study identified 1116 differentially expressed genes at one or more time points and 1677 genes with significant temporal expression patterns, defining a 516-gene core temporal host-response signature. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as providing a reproducible strategy for prioritizing host-directed therapeutic candidates against NiV infection, which is novel in leveraging computational methods to identify potential drug candidates before experimental validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for NiV infection by identifying potential host-directed therapeutic candidates. papers.title_zh: 基于时间分辨的宿主转录组学和网络邻近性优先选择针对尼帕病毒感染的宿主导向候选药物
papers.source_body_en: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic henipavirus that causes severe respiratory and neurological disease, yet no specific therapeutics are approved for human NiV infection. Because studies involving live NiV require biosafety level 4 containment and are technically demanding, computational host-directed drug repositioning provides a practical strategy for prioritizing candidates before experimental validation. Using the public NiV infection transcriptomic dataset GSE166707, we developed a time-resolved host-response drug-repositioning framework that integrated time-point differential expression analysis with time-series modeling. Core temporal genes were stratified into host dependency factors, host restriction factors and residual host-response genes using annotations from the Human–Virus Interaction DataBase. Candidate drugs were prioritized by combining Connectivity Map (CMap) reversal analysis, network proximity analysis, literature-curated NiV host-pathway directionality, pharmacological suitability and reported antiviral evidence. Suitable public drug-perturbation transcriptomic datasets were further analyzed by gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) to evaluate their consistency with the predicted reversal directions. We identified 1116 genes differentially expressed at one or more time points and 1677 genes exhibiting significant temporal expression patterns, whose intersection defined a 516-gene core temporal host-response signature comprising 58 host dependency factors, 18 host restriction factors and 440 residual host-response genes. This signature captured a staged transition from early virus-associated recognition to inflammatory signaling, endoplasmic reticulum stress, increased protein-processing demands, and dysregulation of the cell cycle and DNA replication. Integrated screening yielded 38 candidate drugs, from which metformin, fenofibrate, lonafarnib and probenecid were prioritized as host-directed candidates warranting further experimental validation. Gene-level reversal and host-network analyses revealed drug-specific modulation of NiV-associated host programs, while external drug-perturbation GSEA supported selected host-factor reversal patterns for metformin and fenofibrate. Overall, this framework provides a reproducible strategy for prioritizing host-directed therapeutic candidates against NiV infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒,NiV)是一种高致病性的人兽共患病病毒,可引起严重的呼吸系统和神经系统疾病,但目前尚无针对人类尼帕病毒感染的特异性治疗药物。由于涉及活体尼帕病毒的研究需要生物安全四级(BSL-4)的防护措施且技术难度较高,基于计算的宿主导向药物再定位策略为在实验验证前优先选择候选药物提供了可行的方案。利用公开的尼帕病毒感染转录组学数据集GSE166707,我们开发了一个基于时间分辨的宿主响应药物再定位框架,该框架整合了时间点差异表达分析和时间序列建模。通过Human–Virus Interaction DataBase的注释,核心时间基因被分为宿主依赖因子、宿主限制因子和残留的宿主响应基因。候选药物的优先级通过结合Connectivity Map(CMap)逆向分析、网络邻近性分析、文献整理的尼帕病毒宿主通路方向性、药理学适宜性以及已报道的抗病毒药物证据进行评估。进一步利用基因集富集分析(GSEA)对合适的公开药物扰动转录组学数据集进行分析,以评估其与预测逆向方向的一致性。我们鉴定了1116个在至少一个时间点差异表达的基因,以及1677个表现出显著时间表达模式的基因,其交集定义了一个包含516个基因的核心时间宿主响应特征,其中包括58个宿主依赖因子、18个宿主限制因子和440个残留的宿主响应基因。该特征捕捉了从早期病毒相关识别到炎症信号、内质网应激、蛋白质加工需求增加以及细胞周期和DNA复制失调的阶段性转变。综合筛选共获得38个候选药物,其中二甲双胍(metformin)、非诺贝特(fenofibrate)、洛纳法瑞宾(lonafarnib)和丙磺舒(probenecid)被优先选择为值得进一步实验验证的宿主导向候选药物。基因层面的逆向分析和宿主网络分析揭示了药物对尼帕病毒相关宿主程序的特异性调控,而外部药物扰动的GSEA支持了二甲双胍和非诺贝特的宿主因子逆向模式。总体而言,该框架为优先选择针对尼帕病毒感染的宿主导向治疗候选药物提供了一个可重复的策略。

papers.title: Analysis of a Mathematical Model of Nipah Virus Transmission with the Influence of Biosecurity Measures on Farms
papers.abstract: Nipah virus causes a zoonotic disease and can be transmitted from animals to humans through contaminated food or through human-to-human transmission. The complexity of Nipah virus transmission among populations highlights the need for control strategies that can curb the spread of the virus within the affected populations. This study aims to determine the effect of biosecurity measures on the spread of the Nipah virus among humans, pigs, and bats. The SEITR mathematical model was selected for the human population, the SIR model for the pig population, and the SI model for the bat population. The mathematical models were analyzed by determining the disease-free equilibrium (DFE) and the basic reproduction number (R0) using the next-generation matrix (NGM) method, local stability analysis, sensitivity analysis, and numerical simulations with variations in the biosecurity implementation level and the transmission rate from infected pigs to humans 4. The results show that the local stability of the DFE depends on the value of R0, with the DFE being locally asymptotically stable when R0 1. Sensitivity analysis and numerical simulations further indicate that a higher level of biosecurity implementation can reduce the potential spread of Nipah virus. Further numerical simulations show that the dynamics of Nipah virus transmission depend on the interaction between transmission, demographic, and biosecurity parameters. These findings underscore the importance of biosecurity measures in controlling Nipah virus transmission while accounting for transmission dynamics within bat populations.
papers.journal: CAUCHY Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of biosecurity measures on the transmission dynamics of Nipah virus among humans, pigs, and bats using mathematical models. The research highlights the need for targeted control strategies due to the complexity of Nipah virus transmission. The SEITR model was used for humans, the SIR model for pigs, and the SI model for bats. The analysis focused on disease-free equilibrium (DFE) and basic reproduction number (R0), revealing that the DFE is locally asymptotically stable when R0 < 1. Sensitivity analysis and numerical simulations demonstrated that increased biosecurity implementation can reduce the potential spread of the virus. The study emphasizes the importance of biosecurity in controlling Nipah virus transmission, particularly in the context of bat populations. The evidence is strong, as it is based on mathematical modeling and simulation techniques, but the findings are limited to theoretical insights rather than empirical data.

papers.title: Structure-guided design of a dual-antigen mRNA vaccine conferring broad protection against Henipaviruses
papers.abstract: Henipaviruses (HNVs), including Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV), are zoonotic paramyxoviruses with high case fatality rates and pandemic potential. Despite their threat, no licensed vaccines are currently available for human use. Here, we present a structure-guided mRNA vaccine strategy that overcomes key challenges in antigen stability, fusogenicity, and cross-protective efficacy. Using rationally engineered NiV F glycoproteins stabilized in the prefusion conformation, we identify a lead candidate (F-205) that abolishes syncytium formation and elicits high prefusion-specific antibody titers. Through systematic combinatorial screening, we determine that co-delivery of F-205 (NiV-M) and G (NiV-B) antigens via mRNA–lipid nanoparticles induces potent neutralizing and cellular immune responses. In stringent golden hamster challenge models, this vaccine confers complete survival against lethal NiV-M, NiV-B and HeV challenge, with viral RNA undetectable in lung, spleen and brain after NiV challenge and significantly reduced viral burden after HeV challenge. We also introduce surrogate assays to assess F conformation and fusion activity under standard biosafety conditions, enabling iterative antigen optimization without live-virus handling. This study defines a broadly protective, mechanistically informed vaccine platform for HNVs and provides a generalizable framework for rational design of mRNA vaccines targeting class I fusion viruses.

papers.title_zh: 基于结构设计的双抗原mRNA 疫苗,可广泛保护免受亨尼帕病毒感染
papers.source_body_en: Henipaviruses (HNVs), including Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV), are zoonotic paramyxoviruses with high case fatality rates and pandemic potential. Despite their threat, no licensed vaccines are currently available for human use. Here, we present a structure-guided mRNA vaccine strategy that overcomes key challenges in antigen stability, fusogenicity, and cross-protective efficacy. Using rationally engineered NiV F glycoproteins stabilized in the prefusion conformation, we identify a lead candidate (F-205) that abolishes syncytium formation and elicits high prefusion-specific antibody titers. Through systematic combinatorial screening, we determine that co-delivery of F-205 (NiV-M) and G (NiV-B) antigens via mRNA–lipid nanoparticles induces potent neutralizing and cellular immune responses. In stringent golden hamster challenge models, this vaccine confers complete survival against lethal NiV-M, NiV-B and HeV challenge, with viral RNA undetectable in lung, spleen and brain after NiV challenge and significantly reduced viral burden after HeV challenge. We also introduce surrogate assays to assess F conformation and fusion activity under standard biosafety conditions, enabling iterative antigen optimization without live-virus handling. This study defines a broadly protective, mechanistically informed vaccine platform for HNVs and provides a generalizable framework for rational design of mRNA vaccines targeting class I fusion viruses.
papers.abstract_zh: 亨尼帕病毒(HNVs),包括尼帕病毒(NiV)和亨尼帕病毒(HeV),是具有高病死率和大流行潜力的人兽共患病性副粘病毒。尽管它们构成重大威胁,但目前尚无针对人类使用的批准疫苗。在此,我们提出了一种基于结构的mRNA 疫苗策略,克服了抗原稳定性、融合活性和交叉保护效果等关键挑战。通过合理设计的NiV F糖蛋白在前融合构象中稳定,我们鉴定出一个先导候选物(F-205),其可消除合胞体形成并诱导高前融合特异性抗体滴度。通过系统的组合筛选,我们确定通过mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒共递送F-205(NiV-M)和G(NiV-B)抗原可诱导强效中和和细胞免疫应答。在严格的金hamster挑战模型中,这种疫苗可完全保护宿主免受致命NiV-M、NiV-B和HeV感染,NiV感染后肺、脾和脑中未检测到病毒RNA,HeV感染后病毒载量显著降低。我们还引入了替代检测方法,以在标准生物安全条件下评估F的构象和融合活性,从而在不使用活病毒的情况下实现抗原的迭代优化。本研究定义了一种广泛保护、基于机制的疫苗平台,用于HNVs,并为针对I类融合病毒的mRNA 疫苗的理性设计提供了可推广的框架。

papers.title: NAT10‐Mediated Acetylation of the Matrix Protein Facilitates Henipavirus and Parahenipavirus Budding by Enhancing Lipid Binding
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic pathogen, yet the host machinery regulating its budding remains poorly defined. Here, the acetyltransferase NAT10 is identified as a critical driver of NiV budding. It is shown that NAT10‐mediated acetylation of the matrix (M) protein at Lysine 248 (K248) promotes viral budding. This modification enhances M affinity for the host phosphoinositide PI(4,5)P2, thereby promoting membrane recruitment and subsequent progeny release. Importantly, this regulatory mechanism is highly conserved; not only do NAT10 orthologs from multiple susceptible hosts (e.g., fruit bat, and pig) consistently support NiV budding, but the NAT10‐M axis also functions across both Henipavirus and Parahenipavirus genera. Crucially, small‐molecule inhibitor of NAT10 significantly suppresses viral budding, highlighting this regulatory axis as a promising antiviral target against these high‐threat viruses.

papers.title: DeepMolVir: Learning Virtual Virus Representations for Sequence-Aware Virus-Inhibitor Activity Prediction.
papers.abstract: The growing threat of emerging and drug-resistant viruses demands efficient approaches for predicting virus-inhibitor interactions. However, most existing computational models treat viruses as categorical identifiers and fail to capture sequence-level biological information. Here, we assembled a data set of 50,711 compound-virus activity pairs spanning 178 viral species and explored protein language models as a strategy for viral representation learning. Using embeddings generated by ESMC-600M, we introduce a virtual virus representation in which viruses are encoded as sequence-derived biological entities rather than as taxonomic labels. These viral representations are integrated with molecular features to model compound-virus interactions. In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Notably, virtual virus representations consistently outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, while ablation studies highlighted viral sequence information as a key contributor to the model performance. Case studies on Nipah virus and hantaviruses further demonstrated the ability of DeepMolVir to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing. Collectively, our findings establish protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction and provide a foundation for computational antiviral discovery. Code and data are available at GitHub: https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 新兴和耐药病毒日益增长的威胁要求高效的方法来预测病毒-抑制剂相互作用。大多数现有的计算模型将病毒视为分类标识符,未能捕捉序列层面的生物学信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们构建了一个包含50,711个化合物-病毒活性对的数据集,涵盖178种病毒物种,并探索了蛋白质语言模型作为病毒表示学习的策略。
elements_zh.methods: 利用由ESMC-600M生成的嵌入,我们引入了一种虚拟病毒表示方法,其中病毒被编码为由序列衍生的生物学实体,而非分类学标签。这些病毒表示与分子特征相结合,以建模化合物-病毒相互作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 在广泛的5折交叉验证中,DeepMolVir表现出强大的预测性能,达到了AUC为0.8653和RMSE为0.9480。对尼帕病毒和汉坦病毒的案例研究进一步证明了DeepMolVir识别候选抗病毒药物骨架和支持跨家族药物再利用的能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些病毒表示始终优于常规基于分类学的编码方法,而消融研究突显了病毒序列信息对模型性能的关键贡献。我们的研究结果确立了基于蛋白质语言模型的病毒表示学习作为序列感知抗病毒药物活性预测的有效策略,并为计算抗病毒药物发现奠定了基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: DeepMolVir识别候选抗病毒药物骨架和支持跨家族药物再利用的能力,可以为监测、诊断和治疗的病毒性感染提供信息,特别是针对新兴和耐药病毒。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 值得注意的是,该研究依赖于大量化合物-病毒活性对的数据集,这可能会限制其泛化能力。然而,模型在交叉验证和案例研究中的表现提供了其有效性的有力证据。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The growing threat of emerging and drug-resistant viruses demands efficient approaches for predicting virus-inhibitor interactions. Most existing computational models treat viruses as categorical identifiers and fail to capture sequence-level biological information.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: Here, we assembled a data set of 50,711 compound-virus activity pairs spanning 178 viral species and explored protein language models as a strategy for viral representation learning.
analysis_en.methods: Using embeddings generated by ESMC-600M, we introduce a virtual virus representation in which viruses are encoded as sequence-derived biological entities rather than as taxonomic labels. These viral representations are integrated with molecular features to model compound-virus interactions.
analysis_en.main_results: In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Case studies on Nipah virus and hantaviruses further demonstrated the ability of DeepMolVir to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: These viral representations consistently outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, while ablation studies highlighted viral sequence information as a key contributor to the model performance. Our findings establish protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction and provide a foundation for computational antiviral discovery.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: DeepMolVir's ability to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of viral infections, particularly for emerging and drug-resistant viruses.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Notably, the study's reliance on a large dataset of compound-virus activity pairs may limit generalizability. However, the model's performance in cross-validation and case studies provides strong evidence for its utility.

papers.title_zh: DeepMolVir:基于蛋白质语言模型学习虚拟病毒表示以实现序列感知的病毒-抑制剂活性预测
papers.source_body_en: The growing threat of emerging and drug-resistant viruses demands efficient approaches for predicting virus-inhibitor interactions. However, most existing computational models treat viruses as categorical identifiers and fail to capture sequence-level biological information. Here, we assembled a data set of 50,711 compound-virus activity pairs spanning 178 viral species and explored protein language models as a strategy for viral representation learning. Using embeddings generated by ESMC-600M, we introduce a virtual virus representation in which viruses are encoded as sequence-derived biological entities rather than as taxonomic labels. These viral representations are integrated with molecular features to model compound-virus interactions. In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Notably, virtual virus representations consistently outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, while ablation studies highlighted viral sequence information as a key contributor to the model performance. Case studies on Nipah virus and hantaviruses further demonstrated the ability of DeepMolVir to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing. Collectively, our findings establish protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction and provide a foundation for computational antiviral discovery. Code and data are available at GitHub: https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir.
papers.abstract_zh: 新兴和耐药病毒日益增长的威胁要求高效的方法来预测病毒-抑制剂相互作用。然而,大多数现有的计算模型将病毒视为分类标识符,未能捕捉序列层面的生物学信息。在这里,我们构建了一个包含50,711个化合物-病毒活性对的数据集,涵盖178种病毒物种,并探索了蛋白质语言模型作为病毒表示学习的策略。利用由ESMC-600M生成的嵌入,我们引入了一种虚拟病毒表示方法,其中病毒被编码为由序列衍生的生物学实体,而非分类学标签。这些病毒表示与分子特征相结合,以建模化合物-病毒相互作用。在广泛的5折交叉验证中,DeepMolVir表现出强大的预测性能,达到了AUC为0.8653和RMSE为0.9480。值得注意的是,虚拟病毒表示方法在常规基于分类学的编码方法上始终表现更优,而消融研究突显了病毒序列信息对模型性能的关键贡献。对尼帕病毒和汉坦病毒的案例研究进一步证明了DeepMolVir识别候选抗病毒药物骨架和支持跨家族药物再利用的能力。总体而言,我们的研究结果确立了基于蛋白质语言模型的病毒表示学习作为序列感知抗病毒药物活性预测的有效策略,并为计算抗病毒药物发现奠定了基础。代码和数据可在GitHub上获取:https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir。
